## Overview

AVERROES (ClinicalTrials.gov number NCT00496769) randomly assigned 5,599 patients with atrial fibrillation who were at increased risk for stroke and for whom vitamin K antagonist therapy was unsuitable to [apixaban](./apixaban.md) 5 mg twice daily or [aspirin](./aspirin.md) 81 to 324 mg per day, with a mean follow-up of 1.1 years. The primary outcome was the occurrence of stroke or systemic embolism; 40% of patients had used a vitamin K antagonist before enrollment ([src_ee77d1914d18a5ece9857b4e40a81405](viking://user/ulab0001/resources/p/pmed01/sources/src_ee77d1914d18a5ece9857b4e40a81405.md)).

## Reported results

The data and safety monitoring board recommended early termination because of a clear benefit in favor of apixaban. There were 51 primary outcome events (1.6% per year) with apixaban and 113 (3.7% per year) with aspirin (hazard ratio 0.45; 95% CI 0.32 to 0.62; P<0.001). Major bleeding occurred at 1.4% versus 1.2% per year and the risk of a first hospitalization for cardiovascular causes was reduced with apixaban (12.6% versus 15.9% per year, P<0.001) ([src_ee77d1914d18a5ece9857b4e40a81405](viking://user/ulab0001/resources/p/pmed01/sources/src_ee77d1914d18a5ece9857b4e40a81405.md)).

The trial was funded by Bristol-Myers Squibb and [Pfizer](./pfizer.md) ([src_ee77d1914d18a5ece9857b4e40a81405](viking://user/ulab0001/resources/p/pmed01/sources/src_ee77d1914d18a5ece9857b4e40a81405.md)).
